items.title: Trump’s Whirlwind Asia Trip Begins in the Philippines
items.summary: President Trump’s 48-hour trip started with a meeting with Southeast Asian leaders in Manila. He will later meet Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir Putin of Russia in Shenzhen, a Chinese economic hub.
items.full_text: President Trump sets off this week for meetings in Asia that will culminate in a summit with two strongmen he has often praised: President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia. It will be the first time the three men, who command the world’s largest nuclear arsenals, will have sat down together. Mr. Trump plans to discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world and the war against Iran, according to a White House spokeswoman. He is not expected to bring up Russia’s war with Ukraine. The brief itinerary appears to reflect Mr. Trump’s preferences. He dislikes big summits where he often is not the sole subject of attention. And he enjoys meeting with leaders of powerful nations — especially Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin, two authoritarian leaders he often talks about in admiring terms. Mr. Trump will be meeting Mr. Xi for the third time this year, and a three-way meeting between China, Russia and the United States would be the first of its kind. On Tuesday, Mr. Trump caught the end of a dayslong meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, after issuing tariffs on countries across the region, even allies. Those moves added to a sentiment in Asia that the United States was not a reliable partner but rather one that treasured its commercial interests over its security interests. The only event of substance on the president’s schedule on Tuesday — signing what he had called a “ trade deal ” with Thailand — did not happen because Mr. Trump said it was still being finalized. Mr. Trump met with leaders from the so-called Quad — the United States, India, Japan and Australia — soon after his arrival. All three partners are smarting from high energy prices triggered by the Iran war, a conflict Mr. Trump never discussed with them before launching it in late February. In Shenzhen — the heart of China’s robotics and artificial intelligence industries — Mr. Trump will pursue détente with Mr. Xi. He needs to extend a soon-expiring trade truce that limited tariffs on Chinese goods entering the United States in return for a Chinese commitment not to cut off rare earths and magnets. Then comes the main event: the meeting with Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin. Referring to the trilateral meeting, Mr. Trump told reporters before leaving Washington: “We are going to be talking about denuclearization, a tough subject because it is very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” Chinese officials have made clear they are not interested in nuclear talks until their arsenal is roughly the size of the American one. Mr. Trump also said, “We will talk about Iran a little,” insisting the situation was in “very good shape.” Analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will make any progress on Iran, with Russia happy to see energy prices elevated since the war began, and China eager to see them rapidly decline. Here’s what else we’re covering: Protests: Thousands of demonstrators assembled in downtown Manila on Tuesday in opposition to Mr. Trump’s visit and to a U.S.-led initiative called Pax Silica, which aims to unite partners around A.I. supply chains independent of China. Read more › North Korea: Mr. Putin could meet with Kim Jong-un if the North Korean leader also travels to China for the APEC summit, Russian state news agencies reported, citing the Kremlin’s spokesman. It was not clear whether Mr. Kim would attend the summit. Ukraine: Mr. Trump also said he would talk about Ukraine, on which Mr. Putin’s aides are engaging in talks with the U.S. and Ukrainian officials, but also renewing demands that NATO pull back its troops to where they were before the alliance expanded toward Russia. Mr. Putin and Mr. Kim have publicly met three times since 2022, and North Korea has been a key supporter of Russia’s military actions in Ukraine. As the war in Ukraine nears its fifth anniversary, with no end in sight, the Kremlin is expected to use Mr. Putin’s many meetings at the APEC summit to showcase how Russia is regarded as one of the major international powers alongside the United States and China. A visit by Mr. Kim would be a rare foray outside North Korea for the leader, and it would further raise the prospect that he could meet with President Trump in China. On the first day of his 48-hour trip to Asia, Mr. Trump told reporters that Mr. Kim “would like” to come to the APEC summit. The president has repeatedly said he would like to meet with Mr. Kim again. On Wednesday, Mr. Putin is scheduled to meet with Xi Jinping, China’s leader. On Thursday, he is set to take part in a trilateral summit with Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump, the first meeting of its kind. The Kremlin said on Monday that it was working to arrange a bilateral meeting between Mr. Putin and Mr. Trump. Before his departure for China, Mr. Putin met on Monday in the Kremlin with Jo Yong-won, a secretary of North Korea’s ruling Workers’ Party. During the meeting, Mr. Putin said that North Korea’s help in driving Ukrainian forces from the Kursk region of Russia last year “marked a new chapter in the history of military cooperation between our countries.” Moscow planned to unveil a monument in Kursk by the end of the year to honor the North Korean troops, Mr. Putin said. The dissonance comes amid growing signs within ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, that the United States is not a reliable partner . The meeting between Mr. Trump and Mr. Anutin is taking place on the sidelines of an ASEAN summit. For more than a year, Washington and Bangkok have been negotiating a new trade agreement that covers items like tariffs, food imports and labor rights. Last year, the United States battered Thailand with a 36 percent tariff, one of the steepest rates levied by Mr. Trump after his return to office. The United States is one of Thailand’s largest export markets, including for goods like pet food . Mr. Trump later reduced the tariffs to 19 percent, before the U.S. Supreme Court struck them down in February. The administration eventually found a way to still impose 12.5 percent tariffs on Thai goods. The signing of a U.S.-Thai trade deal might still be far off, requiring Thailand’s parliament to pass a law, but the meeting delivers an easy publicity win for Mr. Anutin and Mr. Trump, who is known to revel even in perceived success. Pavida Pananond, an economist at Thammasat Business School in Bangkok, said, “The level of trust Thailand has in the U.S. is not at the same level as before all this economic weaponization of tariffs.” Most of the demonstrators were university students who said that they were fed up with the government, which they said was more focused on preserving its relationship with the United States than helping impoverished Filipinos. Cinna Sison, 18, who studies European languages at the University of the Philippines, said they were inspired by the recent mass protests in France . “I love the French,” she said. “They know how to protest.” Ms. Sison said she had worn colorful makeup to mark her first time attending a demonstration. “I am here to show my solidarity with fellow young activists. We are here to show our disgust to the fascist Trump and to Marcos for kowtowing to his every wish,” she said, referring to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. of the Philippines. Mr. Trump is expected to hold a bilateral meeting with Mr. Marcos on Wednesday before he heads to China for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The Philippine president, who earlier this year described Washington as a “steadfast partner,” has said little publicly about meeting Mr. Trump. His administration has hinted that the two sides are working on a military aid agreement. In Manila, Ms. Sison wore a red scarf on her head and a red shirt with the words “Silicone not Silica” — a reference to Pax Silica , a U.S.-led consortium of countries aiming to create artificial intelligence supply chains independent of China. Ms. Sison added that Pax Silica was a symbolic return of the Americans to the Philippines, the site of former U.S. military bases , as Washington leaned on a regional ally to counter China. “Neighborliness is important, but it is not important to be subservient to U.S. interests,” she said. Nearby, Raja Bausing, a 22-year-old visual artist, was busy putting the finishing touches on a papier-mâché model of Mr. Trump holding Mr. Marcos. “We want to show how Trump is a warmonger, while Marcos is a lap dog,” she said. “They are very disrespectful to Filipinos. Trump was welcomed in a grand way and yet we Filipinos are maltreated.” APEC The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum is a group of 21 member economies , most of which are from that region. Its members also include Canada, Mexico, Australia, Russia and the United States. It promotes trade in Asia, but is not a free trade bloc. Its leaders meet annually, with the location rotating each year. Meetings between world leaders on the sidelines of the summit can often overshadow the main proceedings. This year, in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, Mr. Trump is expected to meet with President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, as well as with Mr. Xi separately. Last year, when Mr. Trump visited the South Korean city of Gyeongju during the week of the APEC meeting, President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea gave him a replica of a gold crown that researchers believe was worn by an ancient Korean ruler. Mr. Trump also met with Mr. Xi in the nearby city of Busan, where the two struck a truce in their countries’ trade war. President Trump received gilded gifts from South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, when he visited the country last year. Credit... items.title: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick took a softer line on Nvidia as calls for tougher controls grew.
items.full_text: Nov. 17, 2026, 6:31 p.m. ET Gina Raimondo, the former commerce secretary, spent a lot of time with Jensen Huang, and he wasn’t always happy. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday, Raimondo said the Biden administration put national security first and clearly defined what Nvidia and other chip sellers could and couldn’t sell to China. “This administration hasn’t been like that,” Raimondo said. Instead, she said the Trump administration has been continually shifting its position from preventing sales to allowing sales to taking a 25 percent cut of sales. “You’re either for America’s national security or you’re not — it’s not at a price,” Raimondo said. Credit... Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times Nov. 17, 2026, 6:25 p.m. ET Nvidia’s earnings aren’t the only marquee event for the A.I. industry this week. Today’s results are likely to set a more stable stage for Anthropic to launch its initial public offering tomorrow, with trading in the new public stock to start on Thursday. A tailwind in the market for other A.I. stocks should help investor sentiment for Anthropic. Nov. 17, 2026, 6:15 p.m. ET Speaking at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Lisa Su, the chief executive of AMD, Nvidia’s largest rival, said that people watching Jensen Huang’s effort should separate “from the noise,” which will “work itself out in time.” “Jensen has been a tremendous leader for the industry,” she said. Her remarks speak to a concern rippling across the industry. Over the past three years, Huang has become the chip industry’s biggest cheerleader, helping breath life into the oldest segment of Silicon Valley. Everyone is wondering what a future looks like without him. Nov. 17, 2026, 6:07 p.m. ET For investors, that went about as well as it could have. Strong earnings for the third quarter that beat expectations. Strong guidance for the fourth quarter that beat expectations. And strong guidance through next year, rebuffing concerns that the company was set for a slowdown in 2027. Nvidia’s stock price is higher. Its rivals stock prices are higher. This is likely to now ripple through markets overnight. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:57 p.m. ET At Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference today, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos had a word of advice for Nvidia: “Hire internally.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:51 p.m. ET Colette Kress, the interim chief executive, signed off the call 10 minutes ahead of schedule with no more questions remaining. “Our momentum is real,” she said. “Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We’ve got this.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:48 p.m. ET Nvidia’s stock price appears to have settled down a little bit after some whipsaw movements earlier after the company’s results were released. The stock is roughly 4 percent higher. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:47 p.m. ET When asked about what the changing political landscape means for Nvidia, Kress said that it was important companies work together so that communities understand the opportunities that come with data centers, including jobs and tax revenue. “The demand and what we have in terms of agentic will continue,” she said, not only in 2027 but in 2028, as well. Some Democrats elected in the midterm election have vowed to halt data center development and rein in A.I. companies. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:39 p.m. ET An analyst asked about margin forecasts. “Is there an acceptable rate of margin compression that you could live with?” the analyst asks. Kress said “we feel confident” about keeping margins high. Margins are important because if they fall, profit growth could also still fall even if demand for Nvidia’s chips kept growing. While the company would be selling more of its products, it would be profiting less from each sale. Kress communicated confidence that the company will retain pricing power. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:37 p.m. ET Kress said the leadership of TSMC, the premier chip producer, was in Nvidia’s offices this week and was “fully engaged in helping us.” TSMC, a Taiwanese company that produces about 90 percent of the world’s most advanced chips, is one of Nvidia’s most important business partners. Huang has previously said Nvidia’s business with TSMC was built on his handshake agreements with its leadership. Kress has told investors that the relationship is continuing even without Huang. Credit... Ann Wang/Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:36 p.m. ET The Nvidia board chairman, Harvey C. Jones, said the company is looking at external and internal candidates for chief executive. “The search will be thorough,” he said. “We want to install the C.E.O., the permanent C.E.O., as quickly as possible.” He added they won’t expedite the search “before finding exactly the right person.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:31 p.m. ET Colette Kress said that the company is making employees a priority during this period of leadership transition. “Like every community that’s out there, there are diverse opinions,” she said. “Our employees, though, we believe are committed.” Kress said the company’s leadership has stood up over the past week to prepare for earnings and support employees around the world. “We have the best technologists on the planet with a world class roadmap,” she said. “It’s business as usual.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:30 p.m. ET The first question of the question-and-answer section was not about Jensen Huang or his resignation from Nvidia. Instead, it was about Nvidia’s projection for revenue growth in the next fiscal year. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:29 p.m. ET Gross profit margins are expected to hold above 70 percent, Kress said. Investors have worried that competition will bring down the cost of Nvidia’s chips, lowering these margins. Ms. Kress’s confidence in keeping them up is indicative of expectations that continued demand will allow prices for those chips to remain high. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:29 p.m. ET Ian Buck is joining Colette Kress and Harvey C. Jones on the question-and-answer section of Nvidia’s calls with investors. Buck is a vice president at Nvidia and the inventor of Cuda, a software that allows Nvidia’s chips to be used to train A.I. He is now considered by some to be a front-runner to permanently succeed Huang. Credit... Nvidia, via Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:22 p.m. ET Nvidia’s call with Wall Street analysts today has offered Colette Kress, the company’s interim chief executive, her first chance to speak about the events of the past week. Kress has served as the company’s chief financial officer since joining Nvidia in 2013. She has a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master’s degree in business administration from Southern Methodist University. She previously worked in finance at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco, before joining Nvidia in 2013. Huang interviewed 22 candidates before hiring Kress as chief financial officer. Credit... Nvidia, via Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:21 p.m. ET Harvey C. Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, joined the interim chief executive Colette Kress on the company’s call with investors. Jones joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, the year it was founded, and was previously the chief executive of Synopsys, an early business partner of Nvidia that provided software for designing chips. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:19 p.m. ET Nvidia said it will stop shipping H200 chips to China. Those are the only chips the company can legally sell to China. Jensen Huang fought for months to get permission to sell them to China and struck a deal with President Trump to give the U.S. government a 25 percent cut of sales. But China hasn’t shown much interest in buying them. In the October quarter, the company sold about $2.4 billion in chips to China, a fraction of the company’s $115.8 billion in total revenue for the period. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:11 p.m. ET Gene Munster, a partner at Deepwater Asset Management, a tech investment firm, said, “Going away from Jensen sends a message that the board wants a changed culture.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:10 p.m. ET These higher forecasts are particularly important for investors. The growth that has already happened is staggering, but it’s also quickly digested by the market and investors are focused on what comes next. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:09 p.m. ET Kress projected Nvidia’s revenue will grow 75 percent in the next fiscal year, 5 percent more than the company had predicted in August. Credit... Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images Nov. 17, 2026, 5:08 p.m. ET In her first comments as interim chief executive, Colette Kress said, “Our momentum is real.” She said the company’s commitment to innovate won’t change, nor will it change its commitment to customers, partners and shareholders.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s daughter, a close ally, remains in a senior role at Nvidia.
items.full_text: Nov. 17, 2026, 6:31 p.m. ET Gina Raimondo, the former commerce secretary, spent a lot of time with Jensen Huang, and he wasn’t always happy. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday, Raimondo said the Biden administration put national security first and clearly defined what Nvidia and other chip sellers could and couldn’t sell to China. “This administration hasn’t been like that,” Raimondo said. Instead, she said the Trump administration has been continually shifting its position from preventing sales to allowing sales to taking a 25 percent cut of sales. “You’re either for America’s national security or you’re not — it’s not at a price,” Raimondo said. Credit... Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times Nov. 17, 2026, 6:25 p.m. ET Nvidia’s earnings aren’t the only marquee event for the A.I. industry this week. Today’s results are likely to set a more stable stage for Anthropic to launch its initial public offering tomorrow, with trading in the new public stock to start on Thursday. A tailwind in the market for other A.I. stocks should help investor sentiment for Anthropic. Nov. 17, 2026, 6:15 p.m. ET Speaking at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Lisa Su, the chief executive of AMD, Nvidia’s largest rival, said that people watching Jensen Huang’s effort should separate “from the noise,” which will “work itself out in time.” “Jensen has been a tremendous leader for the industry,” she said. Her remarks speak to a concern rippling across the industry. Over the past three years, Huang has become the chip industry’s biggest cheerleader, helping breath life into the oldest segment of Silicon Valley. Everyone is wondering what a future looks like without him. Nov. 17, 2026, 6:07 p.m. ET For investors, that went about as well as it could have. Strong earnings for the third quarter that beat expectations. Strong guidance for the fourth quarter that beat expectations. And strong guidance through next year, rebuffing concerns that the company was set for a slowdown in 2027. Nvidia’s stock price is higher. Its rivals stock prices are higher. This is likely to now ripple through markets overnight. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:57 p.m. ET At Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference today, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos had a word of advice for Nvidia: “Hire internally.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:51 p.m. ET Colette Kress, the interim chief executive, signed off the call 10 minutes ahead of schedule with no more questions remaining. “Our momentum is real,” she said. “Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We’ve got this.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:48 p.m. ET Nvidia’s stock price appears to have settled down a little bit after some whipsaw movements earlier after the company’s results were released. The stock is roughly 4 percent higher. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:47 p.m. ET When asked about what the changing political landscape means for Nvidia, Kress said that it was important companies work together so that communities understand the opportunities that come with data centers, including jobs and tax revenue. “The demand and what we have in terms of agentic will continue,” she said, not only in 2027 but in 2028, as well. Some Democrats elected in the midterm election have vowed to halt data center development and rein in A.I. companies. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:39 p.m. ET An analyst asked about margin forecasts. “Is there an acceptable rate of margin compression that you could live with?” the analyst asks. Kress said “we feel confident” about keeping margins high. Margins are important because if they fall, profit growth could also still fall even if demand for Nvidia’s chips kept growing. While the company would be selling more of its products, it would be profiting less from each sale. Kress communicated confidence that the company will retain pricing power. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:37 p.m. ET Kress said the leadership of TSMC, the premier chip producer, was in Nvidia’s offices this week and was “fully engaged in helping us.” TSMC, a Taiwanese company that produces about 90 percent of the world’s most advanced chips, is one of Nvidia’s most important business partners. Huang has previously said Nvidia’s business with TSMC was built on his handshake agreements with its leadership. Kress has told investors that the relationship is continuing even without Huang. Credit... Ann Wang/Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:36 p.m. ET The Nvidia board chairman, Harvey C. Jones, said the company is looking at external and internal candidates for chief executive. “The search will be thorough,” he said. “We want to install the C.E.O., the permanent C.E.O., as quickly as possible.” He added they won’t expedite the search “before finding exactly the right person.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:31 p.m. ET Colette Kress said that the company is making employees a priority during this period of leadership transition. “Like every community that’s out there, there are diverse opinions,” she said. “Our employees, though, we believe are committed.” Kress said the company’s leadership has stood up over the past week to prepare for earnings and support employees around the world. “We have the best technologists on the planet with a world class roadmap,” she said. “It’s business as usual.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:30 p.m. ET The first question of the question-and-answer section was not about Jensen Huang or his resignation from Nvidia. Instead, it was about Nvidia’s projection for revenue growth in the next fiscal year. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:29 p.m. ET Gross profit margins are expected to hold above 70 percent, Kress said. Investors have worried that competition will bring down the cost of Nvidia’s chips, lowering these margins. Ms. Kress’s confidence in keeping them up is indicative of expectations that continued demand will allow prices for those chips to remain high. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:29 p.m. ET Ian Buck is joining Colette Kress and Harvey C. Jones on the question-and-answer section of Nvidia’s calls with investors. Buck is a vice president at Nvidia and the inventor of Cuda, a software that allows Nvidia’s chips to be used to train A.I. He is now considered by some to be a front-runner to permanently succeed Huang. Credit... Nvidia, via Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:22 p.m. ET Nvidia’s call with Wall Street analysts today has offered Colette Kress, the company’s interim chief executive, her first chance to speak about the events of the past week. Kress has served as the company’s chief financial officer since joining Nvidia in 2013. She has a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master’s degree in business administration from Southern Methodist University. She previously worked in finance at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco, before joining Nvidia in 2013. Huang interviewed 22 candidates before hiring Kress as chief financial officer. Credit... Nvidia, via Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:21 p.m. ET Harvey C. Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, joined the interim chief executive Colette Kress on the company’s call with investors. Jones joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, the year it was founded, and was previously the chief executive of Synopsys, an early business partner of Nvidia that provided software for designing chips. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:19 p.m. ET Nvidia said it will stop shipping H200 chips to China. Those are the only chips the company can legally sell to China. Jensen Huang fought for months to get permission to sell them to China and struck a deal with President Trump to give the U.S. government a 25 percent cut of sales. But China hasn’t shown much interest in buying them. In the October quarter, the company sold about $2.4 billion in chips to China, a fraction of the company’s $115.8 billion in total revenue for the period. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:11 p.m. ET Gene Munster, a partner at Deepwater Asset Management, a tech investment firm, said, “Going away from Jensen sends a message that the board wants a changed culture.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:10 p.m. ET These higher forecasts are particularly important for investors. The growth that has already happened is staggering, but it’s also quickly digested by the market and investors are focused on what comes next. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:09 p.m. ET Kress projected Nvidia’s revenue will grow 75 percent in the next fiscal year, 5 percent more than the company had predicted in August. Credit... Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images Nov. 17, 2026, 5:08 p.m. ET In her first comments as interim chief executive, Colette Kress said, “Our momentum is real.” She said the company’s commitment to innovate won’t change, nor will it change its commitment to customers, partners and shareholders.

She has a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master’s degree in business administration from Southern Methodist University. She previously worked in finance at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco, before joining Nvidia in 2013. Huang interviewed 22 candidates before hiring Kress as chief financial officer. Credit... Nvidia, via Reuters Nov. 17, 2026, 5:21 p.m. ET Harvey C. Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, joined the interim chief executive Colette Kress on the company’s call with investors. Jones joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, the year it was founded, and was previously the chief executive of Synopsys, an early business partner of Nvidia that provided software for designing chips. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:19 p.m. ET Nvidia said it will stop shipping H200 chips to China. Those are the only chips the company can legally sell to China. Jensen Huang fought for months to get permission to sell them to China and struck a deal with President Trump to give the U.S. government a 25 percent cut of sales. But China hasn’t shown much interest in buying them. In the October quarter, the company sold about $2.4 billion in chips to China, a fraction of the company’s $115.8 billion in total revenue for the period. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:11 p.m. ET Gene Munster, a partner at Deepwater Asset Management, a tech investment firm, said, “Going away from Jensen sends a message that the board wants a changed culture.” Nov. 17, 2026, 5:10 p.m. ET These higher forecasts are particularly important for investors. The growth that has already happened is staggering, but it’s also quickly digested by the market and investors are focused on what comes next. Nov. 17, 2026, 5:09 p.m. ET Kress projected Nvidia’s revenue will grow 75 percent in the next fiscal year, 5 percent more than the company had predicted in August. Credit... Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images Nov. 17, 2026, 5:08 p.m. ET In her first comments as interim chief executive, Colette Kress said, “Our momentum is real.” She said the company’s commitment to innovate won’t change, nor will it change its commitment to customers, partners and shareholders.
